item.text: {"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"During 2023, the federal government translated several priorities into enacted machinery, especially the Bolsa Família redesign: the presidential measure defined objectives, conditionalities, decentralized management, funding arrangements, a federal inspection network, performance-linked transfers, social-control mechanisms, data interoperability, and repayment and anti-fraud procedures (BATCH-0019-E001; BATCH-0019-E003; BATCH-0019-E004; BATCH-0019-E005). It also enacted or established machinery for the Minha Casa, Minha Vida revival, the National Cybersecurity Policy and Committee, Indigenous-affairs institutions and appointments, and a sustainable fiscal regime, while 2023 budget legislation authorized substantial credits for Bolsa Família and other ministries (BATCH-0019-E018; BATCH-0017-E007; BATCH-0017-E008; BATCH-0020-E010; BATCH-0020-E006; BATCH-0005-E022). The translation remained incomplete in period: the PPA primarily governed 2024–2027 rather than 2023 implementation (BATCH-0017-E002), and the supplied evidence does not establish staffing, enforcement, meetings, actual spending, or completed outputs for most new machinery. Audits and contemporaneous assessments also identified weak monitoring and CadÚnico controls, an inoperative sanitation coordination committee, absent strategic planning in teacher training, and design weaknesses in the fiscal framework (BATCH-0003-E009; BATCH-0005-E007; BATCH-0005-E008; BATCH-0018-E002). Attribution is strongest for measures and decrees expressly signed or sponsored by the presidency, but congressional action, subnational execution, inherited systems, and cabinet administration limit personal attribution to
